source_text: Renuntiemus carnalibus, ut aliquando spiritalia retractemus. Rape occasionem, etsi non exoptatissimam, attamen opportunam, non habere cui debitum solveres, et a quo exsolvereris: desiisti esse debitor. O te felicem! dimisisti debitorem; sustine damnum. Quid si, quod diximus damnum, lucrum sentias? Per continentiam enim negotiaberis magnam substantiam sanctitatis; parcimonia carnis, spiritum adquires. Recogitemus enim ipsam conscientiam nostram, quam alium se homo sentiat: cum forte a sua foemina cessat, spiritaliter sapit. Si orationem facit ad Dominum, prope est coelo. Si scripturis incumbit, totus illic est. Si psalmum canit, placet sibi. Si daemonem adjurat, confidit sibi. Ideo Apostolus temporalem purificationem orationum commendandarum caussa adjecit; ut sciremus, quod ad tempus prodest semper nobis exercendum esse, ut semper prosit. Quotidie, imo omni momento oratio hominibus necessaria est, utique et continentia, postquam oratio necessaria est. Oratio de conscientia procedit. Si conscientia erubescat, erubescit oratio. Spiritus deducit orationem ad Deum. Si spiritus reus apud se sit conscientiae erubescentis, quomodo audebit orationem ducere ab illa, de qua erubescente et ipse suffunditur sanctus minister? Etenim est prophetica vox veteris Testamenti: Sancti eritis, quia Deus sanctus; et rursus: Cum sancto sanctificaberis, et cum viro innocente innocens eris, et cum electo electus. Debemus enim ita ingredi in disciplina Domini, ut dignum est, non secundum carnis calentes concupiscentias. Ita enim et Apostolus dicit, quod sapere secundum carnem mors sit; secundum spiritum vero sapere vita aeterna sit in Christo Jesu Domino nostro. Si haec obfusio, etiam cum in unis nuptiis res carnis exercetur, Spiritum Sanctum avertit, quanto magis cum in secundo matrimonio agitur?
pass_a_gloss: Let us renounce carnal things so that at some time we may reconsider spiritual things. Seize the opportunity, even if not the most desired, yet opportune, not having someone to whom you owe a debt and from whom you are released: you have ceased to be a debtor. O you happy one! you have dismissed the debtor; endure the loss. What if, what we said is a loss, you consider a gain? For through continence you will indeed negotiate a great substance of sanctity; by parsimony of the flesh, you acquire the spirit. Let us reconsider our own conscience, which a person feels to be different: when perhaps he ceases from his own wife, he has spiritual understanding. If he makes a prayer to the Lord, he is near heaven. If he devotes himself to the scriptures, he is entirely there. If he sings a psalm, it pleases him. If he adjures a demon, he confides in himself. Therefore the Apostle added a temporary purification of prayers for the sake of commendation; so that we may know what is profitable for the time to be always exercised by us, so that it may always be profitable. Every day, or rather every moment, prayer is necessary for people, and also continence, after prayer is necessary. Prayer proceeds from conscience. If conscience is ashamed, prayer is ashamed. The Spirit leads prayer to God. If the spirit is guilty before its own conscience, which is ashamed, how will it dare to lead prayer from that which, being ashamed, even the holy minister is stained? Indeed there is a prophetic voice of the Old Testament: You will be holy, because God is holy; and again: You will be sanctified with the holy one, and with the innocent man you will be innocent, and with the elect you will be elect. For we ought to enter into the discipline of the Lord in such a way as is worthy, not according to the hot desires of the flesh. For thus also the Apostle says, that to think according to the flesh is death; but to think according to the spirit is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. If this obscuration, even when the thing of the flesh is exercised in single marriage, averts the Holy Spirit, how much more when a second marriage is undertaken?

pass_b_english: Let's renounce carnal things so we might finally reconsider spiritual ones. Seize this opportunity, even if it's not the one you'd most desire—it's still opportune. You no longer owe a debt to anyone, and you've been released from it: you've ceased being a debtor. How fortunate you are! You've dismissed the debtor; now endure the loss. But what if what we call a loss you actually consider a gain? Through continence you'll negotiate a great substance of sanctity; through parsimony of the flesh, you'll acquire the spirit. Let's examine our own conscience, which a person feels to be different from itself: when someone ceases relations with his own wife, he gains spiritual understanding. If he prays to the Lord, he's near heaven. If he devotes himself to the scriptures, he's entirely there. If he sings a psalm, it pleases him. If he adjures a demon, he's confident in himself. That's why the Apostle added a temporary purification for the sake of commending prayers; so we'd know that what's profitable for the time must always be exercised by us, so it'll always be profitable. Every day—nay, every moment—prayer is necessary for people, and continence too, once prayer is necessary. Prayer proceeds from conscience. If conscience is ashamed, prayer is ashamed. The Spirit leads prayer to God. If the spirit is guilty before its own ashamed conscience, how will it dare to lead prayer from that source, when even the holy minister is stained by its shame? For there's a prophetic voice of the Old Testament: "You will be holy, because God is holy" (Leviticus 11:44); and again: "You will be sanctified with the holy one, and with the innocent man you will be innocent, and with the elect you will be elect." We ought to enter the Lord's discipline in a worthy manner, not according to the burning desires of the flesh. For the Apostle also says that to think according to the flesh is death; but to think according to the spirit is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. If this obscuration, even when the fleshly act is exercised within a single marriage, drives away the Holy Spirit, how much more when a second marriage is undertaken?

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. Scripture citations (Leviticus 11:44) are correctly added to the English text to identify the Old Testament allusion as required. The translation of 'obfusio' as 'obscuration' and 'sapere secundum carnem' as 'to think according to the flesh' is faithful to the sense.

source: 'Sancti eritis, quia Deus sanctus; et rursus: Cum sancto sanctificaberis, et cum viro innocente innocens eris, et cum electo electus.' english: 'You will be holy, because God is holy; and again: You will be sanctified with the holy one, and with the innocent man you will be innocent, and with the elect you will be elect.'
reasons: The Pass A translation omits the phrase 'et rursus' (and again) in the quote, which is present in the source text.

The Pass B translation incorrectly cites 'Leviticus 11:44' for the quote 'You will be holy, because God is holy,' which is actually from Leviticus 11:44, but the second quote 'You will be sanctified with the holy one, and with the innocent man you will be innocent, and with the elect you will be elect' is not properly attributed to the correct source in the Pass A translation.
